title: Understanding Boxcar Kernel
text: The boxcar kernel is a simple function used in kernel density estimation. It assigns a constant weight to all points within a certain range and zero weight to points outside that range. The width of this range is determined by the parameter \( \alpha \).

title: Applying the Boxcar Kernel
text: To apply the boxcar kernel, check if the difference \( $$x-x_i$$ \) falls within the range \( -\alpha/2 \leq $$x-x_i$$ \leq \alpha/2 \). If it does, the kernel value is \( 1/\alpha \); otherwise, it is $$0$$.

title: Calculate the Range
text: What is the range of values for \( $$x-x_i$$ \) when \( $$\alpha=2$$ \)?

title: Check Each Age
text: For age $$22.5$$, check if it falls within the range for each given age (20, $$22$$, 23) using the boxcar kernel with \( $$\alpha=2$$ \). Which ages contribute to the density?

title: Calculate the Density
text: The estimated density is the sum of the kernel values for each contributing age divided by the total number of ages. Calculate this sum to find the density at age $$22.5$$.
